watchdogAndResourceVectors.analysis: NativeEngine creates a ClearScript V8ScriptEngine without any execution timeout or background watchdog timer that calls v8.Interrupt(). In clicky-draw-native.js:650, ClickyDraw.live(...) is instantiated without 'sandbox: "worker"' (ClearScript V8 has no Web Worker API anyway) and without 'budgetMs', leaving sink.deadline = 0 (disabled) in clicky-draw-engine.js:1080. Even if budgetMs were passed, checkDeadline (clicky-draw-engine.js:1066-1071) is only checked inside push() when emitting a drawing primitive, never inside a pure JS loop. Consequently, while(true){} inside NativeEngine.Feed, NativeEngine.RenderWhole, or NativeEngine.Evaluate permanently freezes the dedicated DrawingThread and deadlocks any synchronous caller waiting on DrawingThread.Invoke's unguarded ManualResetEventSlim.Wait() (DrawingThread.cs:220).

watchdogAndResourceVectors.examplePayload: const f = scene3d(680, 90, 520, 440, '3D'); f.tick((dt, t) => { while (true) {} });
watchdogAndResourceVectors.analysis: In clicky-draw-native.js:835-851, globalThis.__tickFigures measures elapsed time AFTER fn(dt, t, f.api) returns ('if (nowMs() - t0 > 8.0) { f.tickFn = null; }'). This post-hoc check only drops slow callbacks that return after >8ms; an infinite loop inside f.tick(...) never returns, hanging NativeEngine.RunFigureTicks and freezing DrawingThread permanently.

watchdogAndResourceVectors.examplePayload: ClickyThreeKernel.Build('{"kind":"custom","loop":true}') or huge subdivision segments in clicky-three-parts.js
watchdogAndResourceVectors.analysis: Unlike NativeEngine.cs:145 (which sets MaxOldSpaceSize = 256 MB), ClickyThreeKernel.cs:290 creates new V8ScriptEngine("Clicky 3D kernel", V8ScriptEngineFlags.DisableGlobalMembers) with NO V8RuntimeConstraints (no MaxOldSpaceSize heap cap) and invokes buildFunction.Invoke(false, recipeJson) inside lock(gate) with no execution timeout or interrupt.

NativeEngine.cs:143 sets V8RuntimeConstraints { MaxOldSpaceSize = 256, MaxNewSpaceSize = 32 }. However, when V8 hits the 256 MB old-space limit, ClearScript/V8 either triggers a fatal V8 OOM or leaves the single long-lived V8ScriptEngine instance in an exhausted heap state because NativeEngine.Clear() (lines 296-306) never recreates or resets the V8ScriptEngine.

clicky-draw-native.js:128-167 exposes globalThis.setTimeout, setInterval, and requestAnimationFrame directly backed by __host.schedule(id, delaySec). Neither clicky-draw-native.js nor NativeEngine.ScheduleTimer (lines 859-868) nor DrawingThread.ScheduleTimer (lines 303-312) enforces any cap on active timer count or minimum delay (> 0.001s = 1ms). Worse, setInterval in clicky-draw-native.js:146-156 is implemented as a recursive setTimeout chain that re-schedules on every tick, and NativeEngine.Clear() (lines 296-306) only calls ClickyDraw.clear() without clearing globalThis.setTimeout/setInterval timers registered directly by LLM scripts! A timer flood permanently saturates DrawingThread's message queue and leaks entries in timerCallbacks, NativeEngine.timerTokens, and DrawingThread.timers.

In clicky-draw-engine.js:1057 and 1089, LLM-generated code is compiled via new Function('__api', '__c', 'with (__api) { return eval(__c); }'), which runs in the shared global V8 context where globalThis.__hostRaw (the .NET HostBridge instance added via v8.AddHostObject("__hostRaw", new HostBridge(this)) at NativeEngine.cs:150), globalThis.__host, globalThis.__win, globalThis.clickyCanvas, and engine entry points (__feed, __drainRender, __clear, __tickFigures) are all writable globals! LLM code can: (1) invoke __hostRaw.Schedule(id, sec) / __hostRaw.Cancel(id) to cancel internal engine animation timers or schedule millions of C# CancellationTokenSources; (2) call __hostRaw.PlaySound / Speak / Caption / Prewarm3D in a tight loop; (3) invoke System.Object.GetType() on __hostRaw; and (4) overwrite globalThis.__drainRender, globalThis.__feed, or Object.prototype, corrupting the overlay engine across all future turns until the desktop app is restarted.
